# AI Lab Support and Campus Routing Assistant

> Assistant combining knowledge-base reasoning, constraint-based booking and shortest-path campus routing.

Author: Muhammad Tanveer (Full-Stack AI Automation Engineer)
Contact: mtanveertahir66@gmail.com | https://www.linkedin.com/in/muhammad-tanveer-advenno/
Repository: https://github.com/haddindeve/ai-lab-support-campus-routing
Source availability: implementation held in a private repository; access on request.

## Summary
A campus assistant has to handle genuinely different question types - eligibility rules, room booking constraints, and navigation - each needing a different technique. One model cannot answer all three correctly.

A router directs each request to the right technique: knowledge-base checks for eligibility, constraint satisfaction for booking feasibility, and weighted shortest-path search for navigation. Each answer comes from the method appropriate to it rather than from one general approximation.

## Stack
Language: Python, Techniques: Knowledge base, CSP, graph search, Testing: Automated test suite, Interface: Command-line demonstration

## Capabilities
- Request routing across reasoning techniques
- Rule-based eligibility validation
- Constraint-based booking checks
- Weighted campus shortest-path routing
- Structured response templates

## Outcomes
- Each query class answered by the technique suited to it
- Deterministic, testable behaviour throughout

## FAQ
Q: Why several techniques instead of one model?
A: Eligibility, scheduling and routing are different computational problems. A rule base, a CSP solver and a graph search each answer their own correctly.

Q: What is the CSP used for?
A: Checking whether a requested booking satisfies all room, time and eligibility constraints simultaneously.

Q: How is routing calculated?
A: Weighted shortest-path search over a graph of campus locations.

Q: Is the code available?
A: Private repository.
